description: Returns the solet's authoritative retired-role registry as {registry_version, roles: [...]}, each role carrying role, retired_at, retired_by, reason, successor and the registry_version it was added at (iss_d9c955a2). This is the explicit versioned interface project-solet's content guard binds to: registry_version strictly increases with every retirement, so a consumer caches by version and refetches when it changes. Every read failure is an error, never an empty list; an empty registry is also an error, because the Register-Lead migration seed guarantees at least one row, so empty means the seed has not run. Consumers must fail closed on any error.
embedding_description: Read the versioned set of retired fleet role names, with the reason, date and successor for each, that transports refuse to deliver to and that document guards reject; fails loudly rather than returning an empty set.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: registry_version (integer, the highest row version) and roles (every retired role, ordered by the version it was added at).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Name each retired role with its reason and successor, and state the registry_version so a consumer can tell whether its cached copy is current.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: A read-only call; it never writes.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: retired_role_registry_unavailable: the registry could not be read, a row was malformed, or the registry is empty because its seed has not run. None of these mean that no role is retired.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: Fail closed: a consumer must refuse whatever it was checking rather than proceed with no retired names. Report the error; do not substitute a hard-coded list.
